ui.tagline: Default runtime. Best for chat, code, and content workflows.
ui.description: The general-purpose workspace most bots should use. Includes Claude Code, AI Gen, the Skills CLI, a TypeScript toolchain, and all three Node package managers. Pick this when you don't need anything beyond standard web/Node/AI tooling.

@anthropic-ai/claude-code.blurb: Anthropic's coding assistant runs right inside the workspace.

packs.description: Python 3 + pip + venv + build tooling for native extensions.
packs.agentGuidance: Python 3 is at `python3` (no unversioned `python`). Use `pip3 install --break-system-packages <pkg>` for system-wide installs (this image follows PEP 668), or `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate` for a project-local venv. Native-extension build tools (build-essential, pkg-config, python3-dev) are present, so packages like Pillow, lxml, manim can compile from source if needed.

packs.description: FFmpeg for video/audio encoding and frame-to-MP4 assembly.
packs.agentGuidance: Use `ffmpeg -i <input> <output>` for transcoding, `ffmpeg -framerate <fps> -i frame_%04d.png out.mp4` for frame sequences, and `ffprobe -v quiet -print_format json -show_format -show_streams <file>` to inspect media. The Debian ffmpeg build includes the common codecs (libx264, libvpx, aac); use `-c:v libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p` for broadly-compatible MP4 output.

packs.description: TeX Live (LaTeX) + dvisvgm — needed for MathTex / Tex rendering in animation pipelines and for PDF/SVG math output.
packs.agentGuidance: Compile LaTeX with `pdflatex <file.tex>` or `latex <file.tex>`. The texlive-latex-extra, texlive-fonts-extra, texlive-latex-recommended, texlive-science and tipa packages are included — covering Manim's `MathTex`/`Tex` requirements and most paper-style documents. Use `dvisvgm <file.dvi>` to convert DVI to SVG. First invocation is slow (font cache build); subsequent calls are fast.

packs.description: Xvfb virtual framebuffer + Mesa OpenGL libs — lets headless OpenGL workloads (ManimGL, Blender headless, etc.) render without a real display.
packs.agentGuidance: Wrap OpenGL/GUI commands with `xvfb-run -a <command>` to give them a virtual display (`-a` auto-picks a free server number). For longer pipelines export a persistent display: `Xvfb :99 -screen 0 1920x1080x24 & export DISPLAY=:99`. Required for ManimGL (`manimgl`); not required for Manim CE (`manim`) which renders headlessly via Cairo.

packs.description: Manim Community Edition (manim) + ManimGL (manimlib) — the two leading Python animation engines, with their native Cairo/Pango deps.
packs.agentGuidance: Two engines coexist. Manim CE — `manim -ql <file.py> <SceneClass>` (Cairo-based, headless, default for most agents). ManimGL — `xvfb-run -a manimgl <file.py> <SceneClass>` (OpenGL; the import itself opens a display, so any `manimgl` invocation or even `import manimlib` must be wrapped in `xvfb-run -a` or run with `DISPLAY` set — the xvfb pack provides this). Python import names differ: `import manim` vs `import manimlib`. Renders land in `./media/videos/<file>/<quality>/<SceneClass>.mp4` by default; pass `--media_dir /home/user/artifacts` to redirect into the artifacts mount. Use `-ql` (480p), `-qm` (720p), `-qh` (1080p) to trade speed for quality.

packs.description: Shared system libraries required to run a headless Chrome / Chrome Headless Shell on Debian Bookworm. Installs no browser binary — downstream packs (e.g. remotion) fetch their own Chrome.
packs.agentGuidance: Provides the native shared libraries a headless Chromium needs (NSS, GBM/Mesa, ALSA, ATK + ATK-bridge, Cairo/Pango, X composite/damage/fixes/randr, CUPS, dbus). It installs NO browser binary — tools that drive headless Chrome (Remotion, Puppeteer, Playwright) must download or point at their own Chromium build; this pack only guarantees the OS-level .so dependencies resolve. If a render fails with `error while loading shared libraries: libXXX.so: cannot open shared object file`, the missing library belongs here.

packs.description: Remotion CLI (React/HTML → MP4 video rendering) with a Chrome Headless Shell pre-downloaded at build time and exposed at a fixed, world-readable path so the non-root runtime user can render offline.
packs.agentGuidance: Remotion renders React compositions to MP4 via headless Chrome. The CLI is installed globally (`remotion`). A Chrome Headless Shell is pre-downloaded to the fixed, world-readable path /opt/remotion/chrome-headless-shell (also exported as $CHROME_HEADLESS_SHELL in interactive shells), so renders work offline without the ~150MB first-run download. Remotion has NO env var for the browser path, so you MUST pass it explicitly with the literal path (env vars are not present in non-interactive `commands.run`): `remotion render <entry> <CompositionId> /home/user/artifacts/out.mp4 --browser-executable /opt/remotion/chrome-headless-shell`. Typical flow: scaffold or open a Remotion project (`package.json` with `remotion` + `src/index.ts` calling registerRoot, and a Root that registers <Composition> ids), `npm install`, then render with the flag above. Without `--browser-executable`, Remotion re-downloads Chrome into the project's node_modules/.remotion. System ffmpeg is present (the ffmpeg pack); Remotion also bundles its own. Domain knowledge lives in the `remotion-best-practices` skill (`skills add remotion-best-practices`) — 38 rule files on captions, audio, sequencing, transitions, fonts, etc.

ui.tagline: Adds Python, Manim, Remotion, ffmpeg, and LaTeX on top of General.
ui.description: Everything in General, plus a full code-to-video stack: Python 3.11, Manim Community Edition + ManimGL, Remotion (render React/HTML to MP4 via headless Chrome), ffmpeg, TeX Live, and Xvfb for headless GL rendering. Use this when your bot needs to render math/diagram animations or programmatic React video.

manim.blurb: Render math and diagram animations as MP4.

remotion.blurb: Render React/HTML compositions to MP4 (Chrome Headless Shell pre-installed).

chrome-headless.blurb: Headless-Chrome system libraries that browser-based renderers depend on.

ffmpeg.blurb: Encode and convert video and audio.
